prompt.adult: At the Feast of Dedication in winter, Jesus walked in the temple. According to 10:23, in what part of it?
prompt.child: One winter Jesus was walking in the temple in Jerusalem. Where in the temple was He?
prompt.teen: John 10:23: “And Jesus walked in the temple, in” what place?
prompt.older: According to John 10:23, in what part of the temple did Jesus walk?

verses.text: Now it was the Feast of Dedication in Jerusalem, and it was winter.
And Jesus walked in the temple, in Solomon’s porch.

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 23.
explanation.teen: 10:22 gives the feast and the season; 10:23 says where He walked. Read the end.
explanation.older: It follows “in the temple, in” in 10:23.

teaching.extended_explanation: 10:24 says the Jews surrounded Him there and asked, “How long do You keep us in doubt?”
teaching.takeaway: Jesus walked in the temple, in Solomon’s porch.

prompt.adult: The chief priests and Pharisees asked the officers, “Why have you not brought Him?” What did the officers reply in 7:46?
prompt.child: Some officers were sent to arrest Jesus, but they came back without Him. What did they say?
prompt.older: According to John 7:46, how did the officers explain coming back without Jesus?

choices.text: He escaped before we could reach Him
We could not find Him in the temple
The crowd would not let us near Him
No man ever spoke like this Man!

verses.text: Then the officers came to the chief priests and Pharisees, who said to them, “Why have you not brought Him?”
The officers answered, “No man ever spoke like this Man!”

explanation.child: Look at what the officers said in verse 46.
explanation.teen: 7:45 has the leaders’ question; 7:46 gives the officers’ reply. Read the reply.

teaching.extended_explanation: 7:47 says the Pharisees answered them, “Are you also deceived?”
teaching.takeaway: The officers answered, “No man ever spoke like this Man!”

prompt.adult: Who told Jesus to go into Judea so others could see His works, and yet, according to 7:5, did not believe in Him?
prompt.child: Some people close to Jesus told Him to go to Judea and show His works, but they did not believe in Him. Who were they?
prompt.teen: John 7:5: “For even” who “did not believe in Him”?
prompt.older: According to John 7:3 and 7:5, who urged Jesus to go to Judea without believing in Him?

verses.text: His brothers therefore said to Him, “Depart from here and go into Judea, that Your disciples also may see the works that You are doing.
For even His brothers did not believe in Him.

explanation.adult: Read the start of 7:3 or the middle of 7:5.
explanation.child: Look at the first words of verse 3.
explanation.teen: 7:3 names who spoke and what they urged; 7:5 repeats the speakers. Read either.

teaching.extended_explanation: 7:10 says that after they had gone up to the feast, He also went up, not openly, but as it were in secret.
teaching.takeaway: His brothers said this, for even His brothers did not believe in Him.

prompt.adult: In 8:33 the people said they had never been in bondage to anyone. What did they claim to be?
prompt.child: When Jesus spoke about being made free, some people said they had never been slaves. Whose family did they say they were?
prompt.older: According to John 8:33, what did the crowd say they were, when Jesus spoke of being made free?

verses.text: They answered Him, “We are Abraham’s descendants, and have never been in bondage to anyone. How can You say, ‘You will be made free’?”
They answered and said to Him, “Abraham is our father.” Jesus said to them, “If you were Abraham’s children, you would do the works of Abraham.

explanation.adult: Read the start of their reply in 8:33.
explanation.child: Look at the first words they say in verse 33.
explanation.teen: 8:33 has their claim, then their question. 8:39 says whom they call father. Read the claim.

teaching.extended_explanation: In 8:39 Jesus answered that if they were truly that man’s children, they would do his works.

review.notes: Fruitful stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _fruitful_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: In 10:33 the Jews said they were not stoning Jesus for a good work. For what did they say they would stone Him?
prompt.child: Some people wanted to throw stones at Jesus. They said it was not for a good deed. What reason did they give?
prompt.teen: John 10:33: “For a good work we do not stone You, but” for what?
prompt.older: According to John 10:33, what charge did the Jews give for wanting to stone Jesus?

verses.text: The Jews answered Him, saying, “For a good work we do not stone You, but for blasphemy, and because You, being a Man, make Yourself God.”
Jesus answered them, “Is it not written in your law, ‘I said, “You are gods” ’?

explanation.adult: Read the middle of their words in 10:33.
explanation.child: Look right after “we do not stone You, but” in verse 33.
explanation.teen: 10:33 gives what it was not, then the charge, then a reason. Read the charge.
explanation.older: It follows “we do not stone You, but” in 10:33.

teaching.extended_explanation: 10:33 ends, “because You, being a Man, make Yourself God.” In 10:34 Jesus answers from what is written in their law.
teaching.takeaway: They said they would stone Him for blasphemy.

prompt.adult: In 10:41 many said John performed no sign. How did Jesus describe John in 5:35?
prompt.child: Jesus spoke about John the Baptist to the crowd. What did He compare John to?
prompt.older: Linking John 5:35 with 10:41, what did Jesus call John?

choices.text: the watchman upon the city wall
the last of the great judges
the guard at the temple doors

verses.text: He was the burning and shining lamp, and you were willing for a time to rejoice in his light.
Then many came to Him and said, “John performed no sign, but all the things that John spoke about this Man were true.”

explanation.child: Look at the first words of verse 35.
explanation.teen: 10:41 is the crowd’s view; 5:35 is Jesus’ description, then the people’s response. Read the start.

teaching.extended_explanation: 5:35 adds that the people were willing for a time to rejoice in his light. 10:41 says all that John spoke about this Man was true.
teaching.takeaway: He was the burning and shining lamp.

prompt.adult: In 5:30 Jesus says He judges as He hears. In 7:24, instead of according to appearance, how must the crowd judge?
prompt.child: Jesus told the crowd not to judge by how things look. How did He tell them to judge?
prompt.teen: John 7:24: “Do not judge according to appearance, but judge” how?
prompt.older: Alongside 5:30, where Jesus speaks of His own judging, what does 7:24 tell the crowd?

verses.text: I can of Myself do nothing. As I hear, I judge; and My judgment is righteous, because I do not seek My own will but the will of the Father who sent Me.
Do not judge according to appearance, but judge with righteous judgment.”

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 24.
explanation.teen: 5:30 is the setting; 7:24 gives what not to do, then what to do. Read the end.

teaching.extended_explanation: 5:30 says He does not seek His own will but the will of the Father who sent Him. 7:24 closes His reply to those angry that He made a man well.

prompt.adult: In 7:30 and again in 8:20 no one laid a hand on Jesus. What reason do both verses give?
prompt.child: Twice people wanted to seize Jesus, but no one laid a hand on Him. Why not?
prompt.teen: John 8:20: “and no one laid hands on Him, for” what?
prompt.older: Linking John 7:30 with 8:20, why was Jesus not taken?

choices.text: His hour had not yet come

verses.text: Therefore they sought to take Him; but no one laid a hand on Him, because His hour had not yet come.
These words Jesus spoke in the treasury, as He taught in the temple; and no one laid hands on Him, for His hour had not yet come.

explanation.adult: Read the end of 7:30 or of 8:20.
explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 7:30.
explanation.teen: Both verses say no one took Him, then give the same reason at the end. Read either ending.
explanation.older: It closes 8:20, after “no one laid hands on Him, for.”

teaching.extended_explanation: 7:30 says they sought to take Him. 8:20 says He spoke these words in the treasury as He taught in the temple.
teaching.takeaway: No one laid a hand on Him, because His hour had not yet come.
